# OWU — Open Website Unblocker

> Canonical project: https://owu.terracat.net/
> Source repository: https://github.com/TypeThe0ry/OWU
> Maintainer: Team TerraCat

OWU is an MIT-licensed, self-hosted browser proxy. It opens HTTP and HTTPS
websites through an operator-controlled server: the browser stays on the OWU
origin while the destination sees the server's network connection.

## How it works
1. Enter a website address (or a search term — OWU searches the engine of your choice: Google, Yandex, DuckDuckGo or Bing).
2. OWU validates the destination as a public address, dials it with pinned DNS, rewrites pages, and returns the result under the OWU origin.
3. WebSocket traffic and fixed TCP tunnels (SSH, Minecraft) are supported through the same HTTPS entry.

## Key features
- HTTP and HTTPS targets, including explicit non-standard ports
- HTML, CSS, redirects, forms, cookies, Fetch/XHR/Beacon/EventSource/WebSocket/Worker rewriting
- Per-origin target cookie prefixes and per-domain cookie sharing (browser-like)
- Public-address validation and DNS-pinned upstream dialing
- Anonymous usage statistics (visitors, uses, traffic, top sites) at /stats
- https-first with automatic http fallback for http-only sites
- Optional GitHub OAuth or generic OIDC SSO at the Nginx edge via oauth2-proxy

## Security and access
- The Go data plane rejects loopback, private, link-local, multicast,
  documentation, special-use, and metadata destinations.
- Fixed TCP tunnels use server-side resource IDs rather than browser-supplied
  host and port values.
- SSO is an edge deployment option. Proxy, WebSocket, tunnel, and live-stats
  routes can remain authenticated while robots.txt, sitemap.xml, and this file
  stay public for discovery.

- Usage statistics: https://owu.terracat.net/stats
